questions.question: Q1. In the power-law model η(γ̇) = K·γ̇^(n−1), what does a flow index n < 1 reveal about the ink's rheology?

answers.a: The ink is dilatant (thickens under shear).
answers.b: The ink is shear-thinning, and the log–log plot of η vs γ̇ has slope n−1 < 0.
answers.c: The ink is Newtonian regardless of shear rate.
answers.d: The consistency index K must be negative.

explanations.b: Correct — For n < 1, the exponent (n−1) is negative, so viscosity decreases with increasing shear rate on a line of slope (n−1).
explanations.d: Incorrect — K is always positive; it sets the magnitude of viscosity.

questions.question: Q2. After extrusion, bioink thixotropy is modeled as η(t) = η₀(1 − e^(−t/τ)). Why is the recovery time t₉₀ = τ·ln(10) particularly important for multi-layer printing?

answers.a: It ensures 90% structural recovery before the next layer lands, preventing layer collapse.
answers.b: It is the total time the ink stays in the nozzle.
answers.c: It is the time the ink spends at maximum viscosity.

explanations.a: Correct — If the next layer is deposited before t₉₀, the bottom layer is still too soft and deforms.
explanations.b: Incorrect — That is residence time t_res, a different quantity.
explanations.c: Incorrect — Maximum viscosity is η₀ at t = 0.
explanations.d: Incorrect — Gelation kinetics use Avrami, not thixotropy.

questions.question: Q3. The Avrami exponent m ranges from 1–4 and reflects the nucleation and growth dimensionality. What does m = 2 typically represent in the context of collagen gelation?

answers.b: Three-dimensional isotropic growth with limited nucleation sites.
answers.c: Two-dimensional surface nucleation followed by two-dimensional growth.
answers.d: Purely linear chain polymerization with no branching.

explanations.b: Incorrect — m = 3 or 4 represents three-dimensional scenarios.
explanations.c: Correct — m = 2 describes nucleation on surfaces or one-dimensional growth of two-dimensional objects.
explanations.d: Incorrect — Avrami exponent is geometric, not about chain structure.

questions.question: Q4. The gel point time is t_gel = (ln 2 / k_Av)^(1/m). Temperature shifts k_Av via Arrhenius law: k_Av(T) = k_Av(T_ref)·exp[−(E_a/R)(1/T − 1/T_ref)]. For E_a ≈ 62 kJ/mol, how does a 10°C rise from 27°C to 37°C affect t_gel?

answers.a: t_gel increases because the rate constant decreases.
answers.b: t_gel decreases substantially (roughly halves) because higher T accelerates gelation exponentially.
answers.c: t_gel remains unchanged; temperature does not affect Avrami kinetics.

explanations.a: Incorrect — Higher T raises k_Av, lowering t_gel.
explanations.b: Correct — The Arrhenius exponent with E_a = 62 kJ/mol gives a strong temperature dependence; ~10°C spans roughly a 2× rate change.
explanations.c: Incorrect — Temperature strongly affects k_Av and thus t_gel.
explanations.d: Incorrect — Temperature dependence is exponential via Arrhenius, not linear.

questions.question: Q5. The wall shear rate at the nozzle exit is γ̇_wall = 4v/R. If you decrease nozzle radius from 400 µm to 200 µm while keeping print speed v constant, γ̇_wall changes by what factor?

answers.c: It remains constant because R cancels with other factors.

explanations.a: Incorrect — The change is larger than 2×.
explanations.b: Incorrect — Narrowing the nozzle increases shear rate, not decreases it.
explanations.c: Incorrect — R is in the denominator of the shear rate formula.
explanations.d: Correct — γ̇_wall is inversely proportional to R, so halving R quadruples γ̇.

questions.question: Q6. Cell survival follows S = exp(−k_kill·τ_wall·t_res) where t_res = L_nozzle/v_print. Explain the resolution–viability trade-off: why can't you simultaneously print fine features (narrow nozzle) and keep S > 85%?

answers.a: Fine nozzles increase wall shear stress τ_wall steeply; while finer resolution is possible, the exponential shear-kill term outweighs the benefit.
answers.b: Fine nozzles require slower printing, extending t_res and increasing shear damage.
answers.c: Narrow nozzles reduce ink viscosity, which kills cells faster.
answers.d: Fine nozzles operate at higher k_kill values due to material properties.

explanations.a: Correct — τ_wall ∝ 1/R³, so the exponent in the survival term grows as R³ decreases, causing exponential cell loss.
explanations.b: Incorrect — Faster printing actually worsens shear damage (τ_wall ∝ v).
explanations.c: Incorrect — Nozzle diameter doesn't change ink viscosity; ink viscosity is an input.
explanations.d: Incorrect — k_kill is a constant for a given cell type, independent of nozzle geometry.

questions.question: Q7. Scaffold modulus decays as E(t) = E₀·exp(−(4/3)k_deg·t), not as E(t) = E₀·exp(−k_deg·t). What is the physical origin of the 4/3 exponent?

answers.a: It is an arbitrary empirical fitting constant.
answers.b: It is the ratio of three-dimensional geometry to one-dimensional fiber strength.
answers.c: It arises from the Gibson–Ashby scaling E ∝ ρ^(4/3) for porous materials, where mass ρ decays as exp(−k_deg·t).
answers.d: It comes from the Poisson ratio of the polymer.

explanations.a: Incorrect — The 4/3 is a model-derived constant, not empirical.
explanations.b: Incorrect — Geometry is captured in the porosity model, not this exponent.
explanations.c: Correct — For porous scaffolds, the modulus scales with mass density to the 4/3 power; as M decays exponentially, E decays faster.
explanations.d: Incorrect — Poisson ratio does not enter the degradation kinetics.

questions.question: Q8. Three polymers are ranked by degradation rate: PLGA (0.02/day), PLA (0.002/day), PCL (0.0005/day). Given tissue regeneration times of skin ~21 d, bone ~90 d, and cartilage ~150 d, which pairing is most appropriate to prevent premature mechanical failure?

answers.a: PLGA for cartilage, PLA for bone, PCL for skin.
answers.b: PLGA for skin, PLA for bone, PCL for cartilage.
answers.c: PLA for all tissues — one size fits all.
answers.d: PCL for cartilage, PLA for bone, PLGA for skin.

explanations.a: Incorrect — PLGA (weeks) is too fast for cartilage (months); PCL (years) is far too slow for skin.
explanations.b: Incorrect — PCL degrades over years, far too slow for a cartilage scaffold (months), and PLGA (weeks) is mismatched to the other tissues.
explanations.c: Incorrect — PLA is too fast for cartilage and too slow for skin.
explanations.d: Correct — Match timescales: PLGA fails in ~weeks (skin 21 d ✓), PLA in ~months (bone 90 d ✓), PCL in ~years (cartilage 150 d ✓).

questions.question: Q9. For a bilayer tracheal stent, the Timoshenko formula gives h = 6·Δε·(1+m)² / (κ_printed·φ) where m = h₁/h₂ and φ = 3(1+m)² + (1+mn)(m² + 1/(mn)). If you want to increase the printed curvature κ_printed without changing mismatch strain Δε, what design change accomplishes this?

answers.a: Increase the total bilayer thickness h.
answers.b: Decrease the total bilayer thickness h to increase curvature.
answers.c: Increase the stiffness ratio n = E₁/E₂.
answers.d: Keep both h and m constant; κ_printed cannot be tuned.

explanations.a: Incorrect — Thicker bilayer produces *lower* curvature (h in denominator).
explanations.b: Correct — A thinner bilayer bends more sharply for the same mismatch strain; κ is inversely proportional to h.
explanations.c: Incorrect — The modulus ratio n affects φ but not in a simple monotonic way; the thinnest approach is direct.
explanations.d: Incorrect — κ_printed can be tuned via Δε, layer thickness h, and geometry m.

questions.question: Q10. The three deployment safety gates for a printed stent are R_f > 95%, R_r > 90%, and T_g = 45–50°C. PLA-SMP passes all three (T_g = 58°C, R_f = 97%, R_r = 92%). Which gate would a hypothetical polyester-SMP with T_g = 48°C, R_f = 94%, and R_r = 93% fail?

answers.c: T_g gate only (48°C is too close to 37°C body temperature).
answers.d: Both R_f and T_g gates are marginal but acceptable.

explanations.a: Correct — Shape fixity must be ≥ 95%; at 94%, the stent risks unwanted shape drift during storage.
explanations.b: Incorrect — R_f = 94% falls short of the 95% requirement.
explanations.c: Incorrect — T_g = 48°C is within the safe 45–50°C window (compare to T_g = 58°C for PLA, which has a larger margin).
explanations.d: Incorrect — The R_f gate is not marginal; it is objectively unmet.
